definitions.explanation: So surprising, extreme, or extraordinary that it is difficult to accept as true.

examples.japanese: {信|しん}じ{難|がた}い{話|はなし}だ。
{信|しん}じ{難|がた}いことに、{彼|かれ}は{無傷|むきず}だった。
これほど{短期間|たんきかん}で{成功|せいこう}するとは、{信|しん}じ{難|がた}い{結果|けっか}だ。
examples.english: Succeeding in such a short time is an unbelievable result.

notes:
Formed from {信|しん}じる (to believe) + {難|がた}い (difficult to ~). The suffix ～{難|がた}い attaches to verb stems to express difficulty or impossibility.

USAGE:
The ～{難|がた}い pattern is productive in Japanese: {理解|りかい}し{難|がた}い (hard to understand), {許|ゆる}し{難|がた}い (hard to forgive). {信|しん}じ{難|がた}い is one of the most commonly used combinations. It has a slightly more formal and literary tone than {信|しん}じられない.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {信|しん}じ{難|がた}い{話|はなし} — an unbelievable story
- {信|しん}じ{難|がた}い{結果|けっか} — an incredible result
- {信|しん}じ{難|がた}いことに — incredibly; unbelievably

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {信|しん}じられない — unbelievable; more colloquial and emotional
- {考|かんが}え{難|がた}い — hard to imagine; difficult to conceive
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い — unbearable; difficult to endure
